Evidence: applyTransition writes errorCode: options.errorCode ?? null on EVERY changed transition; only failRun (:139-141) and executor last hop pass a code, so any later hop without one nulls it
Reproduction: Call transition(id, running, reason, E_X) then transition(id, waiting_for_tool, reason) - errorCode becomes null
Root cause: errorCode treated as write-through field instead of sticky diagnostic
Impact: Failure codes erased by any subsequent transition; recovery hops lose the last error. Latent today (no production caller sets errorCode on non-terminal hops) but the port accepts it
Proposed fix: Write errorCode only when explicitly provided (undefined = leave unchanged; null = explicit clear) or document sticky semantics and update callers
Required tests: Unit: transition with errorCode then reason-only hop preserves code; explicit null clears; docs contract row updated

Evidence: cancelRun does two sequential applyTransition calls; second hop null (CAS lost twice / concurrent move) returns null although first hop committed - row stays cancelling
Reproduction: Simulate second update returning [] twice (scripted db) or concurrent writer between hops - cancelRun returns null, row status = cancelling
Root cause: Two-hop cancel is not atomic and result conflates hop-1 outcome with hop-2
Impact: Caller sees cancel failure while row is mid-cancel; eventual consistency via sweep self-heal (orphan-sweep.ts:88-93) delays up to sweep interval. complete/fail/cancel have zero production callers today
Proposed fix: Return first.row (status cancelling) when hop 2 is rejected, or retry hop 2 once; document; add unit test
Required tests: Unit: second-hop rejection - documented outcome; sweep heals cancelling-cancelled

Evidence: Resolver pair threads workspaceId, but NO production caller passes it (grep: zero). Socket creates the row WITH workspaceId (workspace record DB when dual-tier) while every subsequent executor/heartbeat/transition/resume call resolves getDb() (ALS/global). HTTP requests get ALS from the x-workspace-id hook; sockets/workers do not
Reproduction: Deploy per-workspace DBs (registry databaseUrl differs from env URL), send a chat message via socket in bullmq mode: create lands in workspace DB; run-worker getById/transition resolve the global pool - run not found / rejected by state machine; row stays created - swept to resumable - HTTP resume works only when the client sends x-workspace-id
Root cause: Threading is wired inside the repository but never adopted by callers; transport scopes differ (ALS vs none)
Impact: In split-DB deployments: runs invisible to their own executor (run-less execution), resume broken in worker scope, stale rows. Matches documented Gaps note in Runs.md; database.ts threading-is-complete claim overstates it
Proposed fix: Thread workspaceId end-to-end (executor passes its workspaceId to transition/getById/touch*/close walks; state-gate input carries it; resume/undo pass run.workspaceId after lookup) OR resolve handle from the run row. Ship with a routing characterization test first
Required tests: Integration/characterization: two DBs, create threaded, read unthreaded - documented outcome; after fix: same-handle guarantee

Proposed fix: Add max-run-age telemetry/alert or a stall detector; at minimum document the ceiling (partially documented already)

Evidence: Research child runs are created + walked but never heartbeated (executor heartbeat covers only the parent). Evidence: In bullmq mode the research runtime enqueues a REAL runs-queue job per child (comment calls it sub-run trace) with runId=childId and userInput=subQ; run-worker executes every job via runtimeGate.execute, which adopts the same child row (already running) and runs a full duplicate runtime for the sub-question - while the parent also executes the search inline.
